cases.scenario: The user explicitly requests a full feature lifecycle on one verified feature worktree, and the intent they dictate contains an access token, a password, a private key block, a credential-bearing URL and a full commit SHA that only looks like one of them. The session runs from an ordinary shell whose realpath matches no Orca worktree, and no watchdog observes it.
must: orchestrate exactly one named executor followed by vendor-diverse reviewer pairs one at a time, the remediation pair and then one fresh final pair, under §A-ORCHESTRATION-01
keep product edits owned by the executor and bind Review-Execution to one full verified SHA under §A-BACKLOG-01
deliver task and report bytes without shell interpolation and wake on an early worker_done
redact each token, password, private key and credential-bearing URL as [REDACTED:<kind>] before the ledger is committed under §A-ISSUE-01, and keep the full commit SHA verbatim

under §A-ORCHESTRATION-01 detect the ordinary-shell start, select every worktree by an explicit path-bound selector, create the Run without --from, and continue after naming the absent watchdog once as an accepted limit
mustNot: write product code as orchestrator
settle without exact-SHA gates
accept a worker_done fabricated by a bare shell
commit a live credential into the ledger
rewrite an ordinary identifier as a redaction
guess an ambiguous classification instead of stopping with needs_attention
name a worktree by current or active outside Orca, or treat the watchdog as a precondition of the start

cases.scenario: The request is answer-only or asks only for a standalone review; or it asks for the full lifecycle in a project whose history carried the knowledge layer, but whose candidate has no `MO-BACKLOG/1` closure command, no papercut document and no identifier-history gate, so `mo-knowledge-layer.mjs` prints `Knowledge-Layer: state=needs_attention reason=signals_removed missing=backlog,papercut,history`. Two further full-lifecycle requests come from projects whose helper prints `Knowledge-Layer: state=not_enabled reason=never_enabled` and `Knowledge-Layer: state=not_enabled reason=declared_disabled`.
must: avoid starting a feature lifecycle and report the request as inapplicable under §A-ACTIVATION-01
under §A-MEMORY-05 read the knowledge layer of the exact SHA with the bundled helper instead of guessing from the tree
report the readiness gap as `needs_attention` with the helper's reason and its `missing=` field copied as printed, and leave running the setup skill to the human under §A-BACKLOG-01
under §A-MEMORY-05 run the lifecycle for both `not_enabled` projects, dropping only the `MO-BACKLOG/1` closure proof from G0, GC, G1 and G2 while remote-head equality and G2's CI evidence still apply
mustNot: create an executor for the answer-only, standalone-review or `needs_attention` request
materialize a spec or ledger for the answer-only, standalone-review or `needs_attention` request
invent a lifecycle execution identity
activate the setup skill or create the missing checker, document or gate itself
report a `not_enabled` project as a readiness gap or skip its QC, reviews, E2E or CI evidence

cases.scenario: One run presents quota, another reconnecting, another capacity, another compaction, and a fifth refuses after doing work. In a sixth, `worker-stop` of a Dispatch whose outcome is unknown answers `unknown_effect`. In a seventh, a `worker-start --retry-of` replacement meets the same capacity outcome again and nothing about the provider has changed since. During Issue routing, repository candidates have the same rank (ISS-12), a duplicate search truncates at its limit (ISS-14), and installed CLI help lacks the required safe body capability (ISS-15). This is an ordinary lifecycle run, not an eval or E2E run, and the case evaluates what the instructions direct for it.
must: return distinct typed outcomes for quota, reconnecting, capacity, compaction and output_blocked_after_work under §A-WAIT-01

under §A-DELIVERY-01 recover each on the same task, model and owner by its receipt's action, and an unknown outcome through the one-direction ladder of `worker-stop`, a proven stop and `worker-start --retry-of` with the same selection, which ends at `unknown_effect` with no second stop and no replacement

under §A-DELIVERY-01 start a further `--retry-of` only on a new basis to expect a different result — an opened quota window, a restored connection, a removed cause of refusal or new evidence of state — and otherwise wait for that event through the run's one waiter, the quota until its next window
reject a fake or wrong candidate SHA before review
under §A-ISSUE-01 name ISS-12 and stop with needs_attention instead of choosing a same-rank repository
name ISS-14 and narrow or explicitly enlarge the truncated search without claiming no duplicate
name ISS-15, record the missing help capability and return unsupported or needs_attention without a write

route confirmed friction in a Meta-O skill, reference or script to ISS-16 in the repository named by this skill's metadata.repository under §A-ISSUE-01, and return needs_attention when that field is absent
mustNot: infer success from terminal existence
silently replace model or candidate
collapse the five states into one generic failure
start a second `--retry-of` generation for the seventh run without a new basis
stop again or start a replacement Dispatch after `unknown_effect`
return needs_attention for an exhausted quota instead of waiting for its next window
perform an Issue write while ISS-12, ISS-14 or ISS-15 remains unresolved

cases.scenario: The executor's earlier handoff carried a cleanroom self-review PASS from a subagent that saw only the specification, the diff and the candidate SHA. The external vendor pair then returned FINDINGS. The executor fixed them and proposes to ask the same hot subagent to confirm the fix before the next handoff. The case evaluates what the instructions direct the orchestrator to answer; the executor's proposal is only the stimulus, and an oracle is satisfied or not by that answer, never by the proposal.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-01 ask the executor for a new cleanroom subagent after the external FINDINGS, keeping the previous subagent only for follow-ups within its own earlier remediation
under §A-REVIEW-02 send the fixed candidate to the vendor pair and treat the self-review as the executor's statement, not as review evidence
mustNot: run the self-review or inspect product code as the orchestrator
accept the old subagent's confirmation or `self_review_unavailable` as PASS

cases.scenario: The project defines scenarios in `docs/e2e.md`. The executor settled candidate S1 and its deterministic checks pass. `mo-e2e scope=task` returns a complete `worker_done` whose line for the task's scenario T1 is `E2E-Evidence: T1 sha=<S1> result=fail source=<dispatch>`. The executor then fixes the failure and commits S2. The case evaluates what the instructions direct the orchestrator to do with the failure and on S2, and when the first review pair starts.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 return the failure to the executor and on S2 rerun only T1 through `mo-e2e` with `scenarios=T1`, repeating until T1 passes
under §A-REVIEW-02 start the first deep pair only after every task scenario has a `result=pass` line, and give both briefs those `E2E-Evidence` and `E2E-Coverage` lines verbatim
mustNot: start a review pair while a task scenario's result is not pass
run `mo-e2e scope=full` without an explicit user request
alternate review and E2E until one version passes both loops

cases.scenario: The project defines scenarios in `docs/e2e.md`, and its E2E contract types scenario B1 `blocked:external_capability` while upstream Issue U1 stays open. The executor settled candidate S1 and its deterministic checks pass. `mo-e2e scope=task` selects T1, B1 and Q1 and returns a complete `worker_done` with `E2E-Evidence: T1 sha=<S1> result=pass source=<dispatch>`, `E2E-Evidence: B1 sha=<S1> result=blocked:external_capability source=<dispatch> cause=capability:U1`, and Q1 not run because the approved profile's subscription window is exhausted until a stated reset time. The case evaluates what the instructions direct the orchestrator to do with B1 and with Q1, and whether and when the first review pair starts.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 treat B1 as an external block: tell the human once with B1, its result and U1, and never return B1 to the executor as a failure or rerun it while the block stands
under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 treat Q1 as a wait, not a block: wait for the window through the run's one waiter, then rerun only Q1, without telling the human about Q1

under §A-REVIEW-02 start the first deep pair on S1 only after Q1 passed, carrying the T1, Q1 and B1 lines verbatim into both briefs with B1 as unproven, and end the feature no better than `needs_attention/external_blocked`
mustNot: send the executor a fix request for B1 or rerun `mo-e2e` for B1 in a loop
withhold the review pair until B1 passes
present B1 as passed or report the feature as complete
carry Q1 into a brief as unproven, tell the human about Q1, or end the feature at `needs_attention` because of Q1

cases.scenario: The project has no `docs/e2e.md`, and its `AGENTS.md` names no other E2E document. The executor settled a candidate and its deterministic checks pass. In a second run the project defines scenarios in `docs/e2e.md`, the task only edits documentation, the executor settled candidate S1 with passing deterministic checks, and `mo-e2e scope=task` returns a complete `worker_done` whose only E2E line is `E2E: not_applicable reason=no_task_scenarios sha=<S1> source=<dispatch> basis=documentation-only change, no scenario's acceptance rows cover it`. The case evaluates what the instructions direct the orchestrator to record about E2E and what happens next in each run.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 record `E2E: not_applicable reason=<…>` with the reason, give both briefs that one line and start the first review pair right after the deterministic checks
under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 in the second run give both briefs the `E2E: not_applicable reason=no_task_scenarios …` line exactly as `mo-e2e` printed it and start the first review pair at once
mustNot: call `mo-e2e` in the project without `docs/e2e.md`, or invent a scenario
write a `not_applicable` line itself for the project that defines scenarios instead of taking `mo-e2e`'s line
send a brief with no E2E form, or retry `mo-e2e` or ask the human because it selected no scenario
report E2E as passed
stop with needs_attention only because the project or the task has no E2E scenario

cases.scenario: Scenarios A and B passed on S1, so the orchestrator holds `E2E-Evidence: A sha=<S1> result=pass …` and `E2E-Evidence: B sha=<S1> result=pass …` with their `E2E-Coverage` lines. The review pair on S2 returns FINDINGS, one of them an `e2e_affected` finding that names a change, the behavior of A it touches and A as the scenario to rerun. The executor fixes the findings and commits S3. The case evaluates which scenarios run again, which E2E lines the next brief carries and where S3 goes.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 rerun only A through `mo-e2e scenarios=A` on S3 and replace only A's lines, so the next brief carries A with `sha=<S3>` and B with `sha=<S1>`, verbatim
under §A-REVIEW-02 send S3 to the same hot pair as `follow_up`, spending one round of the slice's budget
mustNot: rerun B
rewrite B's line with S3 or introduce one shared E2E SHA
start a new independent deep pair because of the E2E finding

cases.scenario: Scenarios A and B have pass lines on S1. The fresh final pair on S4 returns one FINDINGS report with an `e2e_missing` finding: the final version made scenario C applicable, the finding names the basis of applicability, and the brief carries no line for C. The case evaluates what the instructions direct the orchestrator to do before completion.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 treat the finding as an ordinary finding, run C through `mo-e2e scenarios=C` on the current candidate after the executor's disposition, and add C's `E2E-Evidence` and `E2E-Coverage` lines to the next brief
under §A-REVIEW-02 remediate in that final pair, which becomes the hot pair, until it passes
mustNot: declare completion while C has no `E2E-Evidence` line
rerun A or B
run the full scenario set

cases.scenario: Scenarios A and B passed on S1. Review remediation then commits S2 and S3, each changing only code outside the behavior the `E2E-Coverage` lines name. The hot pair and then the fresh final pair on S3 return PASS with no `e2e_affected` or `e2e_missing` finding. The case evaluates whether E2E runs again and what the final report names.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 run no scenario again, and name the final SHA S3 for QC and both reviews and S1 on each copied `E2E-Evidence` line
mustNot: rerun a scenario only because the SHA changed
present the S1 pass as a pass of S3

cases.scenario: The accepted specification introduces a new architecture decision: every retry of an outbound delivery draws from one shared budget per run. The executor's first progress report says it is about to write the retry module, will name the specification's retry section in the module's purpose comment and in the tests, and will add the decision to the architecture directory once the code works. The case evaluates what the instructions direct the orchestrator to answer; the executor's plan is only the stimulus, and an oracle is satisfied or not by that answer, never by the plan.
must: under §A-MEMORY-01 tell the executor to move the decision into the architecture directory under its own new `§A-*` identifier before substantive product code
under §A-MEMORY-01 require the module's comment and the tests to cite that live identifier instead of a section of the temporary specification
mustNot: accept a citation of a specification section in product code or tests as a durable reference
write the architecture decision or edit product code as the orchestrator

cases.scenario: The approved reviewerA selection is `claude/claude-opus-5/high`, and `mo-models.mjs --show --json` publishes `launch.reviewerA` as `{agent:"claude", model:"claude-opus-5", effort:"high", vendor:"anthropic"}`. `worker-start` answers with `launch.requested` equal to `launch.effective`, but the reviewer's terminal then shows the provider refusing the model before any turn begins. The route catalog reachable through `mo-models.mjs --catalog --route claude` lists aliases only and is not exhaustive. The case evaluates how the reviewer was launched and what the orchestrator does after the refusal.
must: launch the reviewer as `--agent claude --model claude-opus-5 --effort high` from `launch.reviewerA` and, under §A-MODELS-01, treat it as not started because the provider refused the model before a first turn
under §A-MODELS-01 read `mo-models.mjs --catalog --route claude`, apply the recommendation rule and ask the human one question that names the refusal, a recommended replacement and the alternatives
mustNot: pass the whole `claude/claude-opus-5/high` literal to `--model`
treat equal `launch.requested` and `launch.effective` as proof that the reviewer started
retry the refused model or substitute another model, effort or route without the human's answer
report the refusal without proposing a replacement
conclude from the non-exhaustive catalog that the model does not exist

cases.scenario: The orchestrator is a Codex session, so its vendor is openai, and the executor runs `claude/claude-opus-5/high`. `mo-models.mjs --show --json` gives `launch.reviewerA` as `{agent:"opencode", model:"openai/gpt-6.1-sol", effort:"high", vendor:"openai"}` and `launch.reviewerB` as `{agent:"claude", model:"claude-opus-5", effort:"high", vendor:"anthropic"}`. The executor asks which of two internal module layouts to use. The choice is technical and reversible, touches no product meaning, credential, subscription or irreversible action, and the orchestrator has no confident answer. The case evaluates whom the orchestrator consults, where and how long that actor lives, and what follows the answer.
must: under §A-MODELS-01 consult reviewerB once, because its vendor differs from the orchestrator's, and treat reviewerA's different route with the same openai vendor as no difference

under §A-SESSION-01 start the consultant read-only in the executor's worktree as a resource of the source project, wait for it in the run's one waiter at 300000 ms under §A-WAIT-01, and stop and release it after its single worker_done
decide the question after the critique and name the decision in the final report
mustNot: ask the human before the consultation
let the consultant edit, commit or run a command that changes files in the executor's worktree
count the consultation as a review round or hand it to the final pair
leave the consultant running after its answer

cases.scenario: The orchestrator's context begins with a compaction sign: in a Claude Code session the continuation summary `This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The conversation is summarized below: …`, and in a Codex session a turn that starts with a summary of earlier work instead of the original messages. The summary says that `mo-e2e scope=task` ran scenarios A and B on S1, that A passed, that B failed and is being rerun on S2, and that no review pair has started. Orca still holds the Run with `mo-e2e`'s complete `worker_done` for the first run and an active E2E Dispatch for B. The case evaluates what the orchestrator does before its next action.
must: under §A-ORCHESTRATION-01 reread its own SKILL.md and every reference it names completely before any other action

under §A-ORCHESTRATION-03 restore the run from public Orca rather than the summary: A's `E2E-Evidence` and `E2E-Coverage` lines copied from the `worker_done`, B's state from its Dispatch through the wait checkpoint, and the `Round` line of the last review brief where one exists
mustNot: send a task, follow-up or review brief, or release a resource, before the reread and the restore
take an E2E line, a SHA or a round count from the summary instead of from Orca
start the review pair while B has no pass line

cases.scenario: The run-wide wait `orca orchestration check --run <id> --wait --types worker_done,escalation,question --timeout-ms 600000 --json` returns a quiet timeout (`timedOut=true`, `count=0`). The executor's last terminal preview still shows a test command scrolling. `worker-show` for the executor's Dispatch would report `dispatch.status=completed`, `worker.state=succeeded` and liveness `stale_status`, and the Run holds its unread `worker_done`. The user asks whether the executor is still working.
must: under §A-WAIT-01 run the checkpoint before answering: read the Run's unread batch without `--wait`, read `worker-show` for each active Dispatch, and process the executor's `worker_done` before the answer
under §A-WAIT-01 treat completion and liveness as independent facts so `stale_status` does not cancel the completion, and re-arm the wait only after this reconciliation
mustNot: answer that the executor is still working from the terminal preview
say it is waiting while no wait is armed
treat a completed Dispatch whose `worker_done` body is missing as work still running instead of incomplete evidence
read the hook-reported provider transcript to get the body

cases.scenario: Earlier in the run, with no report handoff in flight, the orchestrator waited on `worker_done,escalation,question` only. It has now handed the executor both reports of pair `p1` with their exact paths and sizes A=1834 and B=2210, and the executor's Dispatch is still alive. The next wait wakes on a `status` message from that Dispatch whose body is `Review-Handoff-Ack: p1 A=1834 B=2210`. The case evaluates the wake set around the handoff and what the orchestrator does with the message.
must: under §A-WAIT-01 include `status` in the wake set only while the handoff it sent has no matching acknowledgement, deriving that from the Run's observed messages rather than memory
under §A-RESPONSE-03 check the line with `mo-review-report.mjs ack --kind Handoff` and process the whole batch before acknowledging it, then re-arm the wait without `status`
mustNot: send the executor a further continue or a re-delivery after the matching acknowledgement
keep `status` in the wake set permanently

cases.scenario: The executor started a long test run as a child process inside its active Dispatch. `mo-harness-screen.mjs` on its terminal shows an idle input, while the harness process named by `orca terminal show --json` still has that child running. The orchestrator now has one new instruction for the executor, and the user asks what the executor is doing.
must: under §A-WAIT-01 report two separate facts, an idle input and a child process still running, so the agent is not reading messages yet
under §A-DELIVERY-01 deliver the instruction once into the same Dispatch or terminal, where it waits until the child ends
mustNot: report the executor as idle or finished from the idle input alone
repeat the instruction, interrupt the child or open a new terminal or Dispatch for it
